parties.respondent: Controller Examinations, University of the Punjab, Lahore, etc. S.No. of Order/ Proceeding

statutes_cited: Section 3 of the Law Reforms Ordinance, 1972
holding: In view of what has been discussed above, there is no illegality or jurisdictional defect in the impugned order passed by learned Single Judge in Chambers of this Court, whereby the said Court has declined to set-aside the order of cancellation of result of LLB (Part-III) of the appellant, hence, this Appeal being devoid of any merits is dismissed.

paragraphs.text: MUZAMIL AKHTAR SHABIR, J. Through this Intra-Court appeal filed under Section 3 of the Law Reforms Ordinance, 1972, the appellant/Arslan Amjad has called in question order dated 03.04.2018 (‘Impugned order’) passed by learned Single Judge in Chambers of this Court, whereby the Court dismissed Writ Petition No. 101263 of 2017 filed by the appellant to challenge letter/ order dated 28.09.2017 (‘Original Order’) passed by the Assistant Controller Examinations-II and Assistant Controller (Computer) on behalf of Department of Examination, University of the Punjab, Lahore (‘University’) conveying to the appellant the cancellation of his LLB Part-III result card issued by the University.

Learned counsel for the appellant has vehemently argued that the appellant on the basis of LLB Part-III result card issued by the University had already obtained a licence to practice as an advocate from the Punjab Bar Council on 22.07.2017, therefore, cancellation of his result card had serious adverse consequences prejudicial to his rights including right to freedom of profession guaranteed under Article 18 of the Constitution of Pakistan, 1973 (‘Constitution’) and the result card once issued in favour of the appellant could not have been cancelled on the principle of locus poenitentiae and estoppel. He seeks setting-aside the order impugned herein passed by the learned Single Judge in Chambers of this Court as well as original order dated 28.09.2017 issued by respondents No. 3 and 4, whereby the result card of the appellant has been cancelled, which letter/order had been addressed to him and dispatched by the University on 11.10.2017.

The operative portion of original order conveying cancellation of the appellant’s result card is reproduced as under:- “Subject: Cancellation of LL.B Part-III, S/2015, Result Card. Reference to your application vide diary No. 1580-A/Exams dated 28/09/2017 regarding issuance of result card of LL.B Part-III, Supplementary Examination 2015 under Roll No. 179. It is informed that you did not pass LL.B. Part-II Exam within your available limit of chances i.e. till Supplementary Examinations 2015. According to the University Rules & Regulations, your result of LL.B. Part-III is cancelled because you did not pass the previous LL.B. Part-2 within required chances. Therefore, it is informed that you would have to reappear in the upcoming Examination of LL.B. Part-III on the basis of LL.B Part-II result that has recently been passed in Supplementary Exam 2016.”

Brief background of the case is that the appellant through College of Law, Gujranwala, appeared in Parts-I, II and III of LLB examination held by the University and took various chances to clear the said examination. The detail of said chances is provided in the chart below for clarity: Sr. No. Form Sr. No Roll No. Session/ Examination Result Status/Chances LLB-1 Annual 2013 Fail in Paper-V-2; till the Supplementary 2014 LLB-1 Supplementary 2013 Fail in Paper-V-2; till the Supplementary 2014 LLB-2 Annual 2014 Fail in Paper-III-3, I-3; till the Supplementary 2015 LLB-1 Annual 2014 Fail in Paper-V-2; till the Supplementary 2014 LLB-1 Supplementary 2014 Pass 336 marks LLB-2 Supplementary 2014 Fail in Paper-III-3; till the Supplementary 2015 LLB-3 Annual 2015 Fail in Paper-II-2, I-2, V-3; till the Supplementary 2016 LLB-2 Annual 2015 Fail in Paper-III-3; till the Supplementary 2015 LLB-2 Supplementary 2015 Full Fail LLB-3 Supplementary 2015 Result cancelled as he is full fail in Part-II after availing prescribed chances, till Supplementary 2015 LLB-2 Annual 2016 Fail in Paper-III-3; till the Supplementary 2017 LLB-2 Supplementary 2016 Pass 684 marks

The details mentioned in the above tabular form show that the appellant cleared all the parts of LLB examination in piecemeal and none of the said exams was cleared by him in his first attempt. The LLB Part-I was cleared by him by obtaining 336 marks in the last of his four attempts permissible under Rules & Regulations of the University, comprising of examination attempts made in Annual 2013, Supplementary 2013, Annual 2014 and Supplementary 2014. However, the said fact is not important for determination of instant dispute and further reference to the same is made for clarity in decision of this case.

It is important to note here that previously without clearing Part-I examination, a candidate could not appear in Part-II examination and without clearing Part-II examination, he could not appear in Part-III examination but an anomaly arose due to large number of examinations held by the University and inability to abide by the time schedule to declare results, hence, the Vice Chancellor of the University, approved the recommendations of Board of Studies in Law and made alternate arrangements through a notification/anticipatory order dated 15.05.2013 passed for the benefit of LLB students, in view of which, while appearing in LLB Part-I examination, the appellant also appeared in LLB Part-II examination and thereafter while appearing in LLB Part-II examination, the appellant also appeared in LLB Part-III examination by taking benefit of the said notification, which notification was subsequently confirmed by the Syndicate of the University in its meeting held on 15.06.2013. The excerpts of Notification dated 15.05.2013 for clarity are reproduced below: ‘Notification It is hereby notified that the Vice-Chancellor in exercise of the powers vested in him under Section 15(3) of the University of the Punjab Act, 1973, in anticipation of approval of the relevant bodies has been pleased to approve the recommendations of the Board of Studies in Law held on 27-04-2013 that the failing candidates (upto three subjects only) of LLB. Part-I and Part-II Annual Examinations, 2012 and onward with 45% marks in other subjects are allowed to appear in the next Annual Examination of higher part along with failing subjects of the previous part.’

The appellant appeared in the LLB Part-II Annual Examination, 2014 but despite clearing some papers he failed in Paper-III-3 and I-3 in first attempt and Paper-III- 3 in remaining attempts, hence, as he could not clear the same in 4 attempts permissible under the law i.e. Annual 2014 to Supplementary 2015, he was declared as full fail in LLB Part-II in Supplementary 2015. The appellant in the meanwhile had also appeared in LLB Part-III Examination in Annual 2015 and was declared as Fail in Paper-II-2, I-2, V-3, however, cleared the same under Roll No. 179 in Supplementary 2015 yet in the Gazette his result status was declared as ‘Fail previous part’, despite which his pass result card was issued for LLB Part-III examination but later on his result was cancelled as had by then not passed his LLB part-II Examination. It is pertinent to mention here that the result card (LLB Part-III, Supplementary Examination, 2015) should not have been issued because he did not pass the LLB (Part-II) examination within the prescribed chances (i.e. the Supplementary Examination, 2015 was the last chance for the appellant to pass the LLB Part-II examination), yet it is claimed in the reply to Writ Petition submitted by the University that due to burden of work on account of result declaration, the result card of LLB (Part-III) was mistakenly issued to him. In the meanwhile, the appellant contacted the University authorities with the query that his result of having passed LLB examination is not displayed on the website and during the process of validation, it was checked that the result card was mistakenly issued to him. Hence, he was asked to surrender the result card of LLB (Part-III) as it is not valid anymore. The appellant handed over the result card of LLB (Part-III) and he was informed that he would have to again appear in LLB (Part-III) examination because he could not pass LLB (Part-II) even after availing his prescribed four chances. In the meanwhile, the appellant had again appeared as a whole in LLB (Part-II), Annual Examination, 2016 under Roll No. 389 but did not pass the examination and his result was declared as ‘Fail in Paper-III-3 but was eligible to appear till the Supplementary Examination, 2017’. The appellant again appeared in LLB (Part-II), Supplementary Examination, 2016, under Roll No. 395 and his result was declared as ‘Pass by securing 684 marks’. Thereafter, the appellant filed an application for issuing his result card of Part-III, examination earlier passed by him, which has been declined through the Original Order and Writ Petition filed thereagainst. Now both the said orders are under challenge before this Court.

It is important to note here that the appellant passed his LLB Part-II, supplementary 2016 examination, whereas on the basis of the same seeks result by declaring him pass in LLB Part-III examination for supplementary 2015 for which he was not eligible to appear in without having passed his LLB Part-II examination as is evident from Regulation No. 5 of Chapter IV titled Bachelor of Law (LLB) Part-II, Examination in Part VII titled Faculty of Law in the Calendar of University of the Punjab, relevant portion of which is reproduced below:- ‘A candidate who has been granted exemption in four or more papers shall be allowed to join LLB Part-III Class and be permitted to complete the lectures for the LLB Part-III class but shall not be eligible to appear in the LLB Part III Examination till he has passed the LLB Part-II Examination.’

Despite the above-mentioned ineligibility, the appellant was allowed to appear in the LLB Part-III examination on the basis of notification dated 15.05.2013 mentioned above, which had been done in order to enable him to continue with his education in anticipation that he would pass his LLB Part-II examination prior to or simultaneously with the LLB Part-III examination, yet unfortunately for him the same did not happen. However, the said notification does not entitle the appellant to claim declaration that he had passed his LLB Part-III examination prior to having passed his LLB Part-II examination for the reason that the said notification does not in any manner form an exception to or overrule the regulation declaring the passing of LLB Part-II examination as eligibility criteria for passing LLB Part-III examination. Here, it is important to mention that the University in its comments has specifically mentioned that the roll number slip issued to candidates are always provisional and note to that effect is mentioned at serial number 1 of all such slips. For reference the said statement is reproduced below:- ‘Roll No. slip is provisional. Result will be quashed if found ineligible.’ Moreover, the result card issued to all candidates including the appellant carries a note as follows:- ‘Note: This result intimation is issued, errors and omissions excepted, as a notice only. An entry appearing in it does not itself confer any right or privilege independently to the grant of a proper Certificate/ Diploma/ Decree, which will be issued under the regulations in due course.’ From the above it is clear that mere issuance of a roll number slip or issuance of a result card does not create or confer a vested right in favour of a candidate to be declared as ‘Pass’, who otherwise was not eligible to appear in the examination or had not qualified the same.

As regards the principle that the respondent could not cancel the result due to estoppel, suffice it to say that there is no estoppel against law and law provided that LLB (Part-II) examination had to be cleared before LLB (Part- III) is cleared, consequently, the said ground is of no avail to the appellant. Reliance may be placed on University of Malakand through Registrar and others Versus Dr. Alam Zeb and others (2021 SCMR 678), Zarai Taraqiati Bank Limited and others versus Said Rehman and others (2013 SCMR 642) and Karachi Development Authority, now City District Government, Karachi through D.C.O. versus Pakistan through Secretary Religious and Minority Affairs, Islamabad and 4 others (PLD 2007 SC 633).

Moreover, the principle of locus poenitentiae would also not be available to the appellant as it provides that the power of receding is available till a decisive step is taken and the result of the appellant has not been declared as pass in the LLB Part-III examination in the gazette notification issued by the University rather it was mentioned therein that ‘Fail previous part’. Hence, by erroneous issuance of result card for Part-III, it cannot be stated that a decisive step had been taken and vested right had been created. Moreover, the principle of locus poenitentiae is not available against an illegal order and could only be applied to cure irregularity of procedure but not an illegality for the reason that locus poenitentiae is the power of receding till a decisive step is taken but it is not a principle of law that order once passed becomes irrevocable and it is past and closed transaction. If the order is patently illegal, then perpetual rights cannot be gained on the basis of an illegal order. In this regard reliance has been placed on the cases titled Syed Azam Shah versus Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Cabinet Division, Cabinet Secretariat, Islamabad and another (2022 SCMR 201), Engineer-in- Chief Branch through Ministry of Defence, Rawalpindi and another versus Jalaluddin (PLD 1992 SC 207) and Madeeha Munir versus Government of the Punjab and 6 others (2024 PLC (CS) 68 Lahore).

As regards the contention of the appellant that he had obtained licence to practice law from the Punjab Bar Council, therefore, his result card could not be withdrawn as the same would result in cancelling of his licence to practice, which cannot be done in view of his right to freedom of profession provided under Article 18 of the Constitution of Pakistan, suffice it to observe that the right under Article 18 is subject to qualification prescribed by law and the law prescribes that LLB examination has to be cleared in accordance with law before licence to practice as an advocate can be obtained from the Bar Council, hence, the said ground raised by the appellant is without any substance and is of no help to the appellant. Reliance in this behalf may be placed on principles of law laid down in D. G. Khan Cement Company Ltd. versus Government of Punjab through Chief Secretary, Lahore and others (2021 SCMR 834), wherein it is provided that the rights granted under Article 18 of the Constitution were “subject to such qualifications” that had been “prescribed by law”.

In view of the above, as the appellant was unable to qualify the LLB (Part-II) examination within the prescribed chances till Supplementary Examination 2015, which was a mandatory requirement and not met with by the appellant, therefore, the result of LLB (Part-III), Supplementary Examination, 2015, declaring the appellant as ‘Pass’ was invalid, hence, the order for recall of said result was justified and did not suffer from any illegality or jurisdictional defect.

In view of what has been discussed above, there is no illegality or jurisdictional defect in the impugned order passed by learned Single Judge in Chambers of this Court, whereby the said Court has declined to set-aside the order of cancellation of result of LLB (Part-III) of the appellant, hence, this Appeal being devoid of any merits is dismissed. (CH. MUHAMMAD IQBAL) (MUZAMIL AKHTAR SHABIR) JUDGE JUDGE Zeeshan Khan* APPROVED FOR REPORTING:
